html:
The festival held every year before Lent in Rio de Janeiro, the largest carnival in the world. The first carnival celebrations in Rio are dated to 1723.

The early custom came from Portugal: the entrudo, a rough street game in which people threw water, flour and mud at each other. In the 1800s the city's elite added masked balls and parades in the European style. Meanwhile poorer, mostly Black Rio developed its own street groups, the cordões and ranchos, with music drawn from African traditions.

The great change came with samba. The first samba school was founded in 1928, and the schools began to compete in parades in the early 1930s. The government of Getúlio Vargas backed them as a symbol of the nation. Since 1984 the main parades have taken place in the Sambadrome. Each school spends a year preparing floats, costumes and a theme song, and thousands march with each one.
